correctness.rationale: Write C=J−2B and expand by nonattacking negative-board rook placements: per C=Σ_j(-2)^j (n−j)!m_j(B). The cyclic row-and-column rotation of order 2^k acts freely on cells; any size-j placement stabilizer has power-of-two order h dividing j, so 2^(k−ν2(j)) divides m_j(B). Legendre ν2((n−j)!)=n−j−s2(n−j), together with s2(n−j)≤k−ν2(j), forces all j=1,...,n−1 terms divisible by 2^n, and j=n has 2^n already. ν2(n!)=n−1. Fourier diagonalization of displacement parity identifies multipliers with these permanents; a balanced unrestricted first-row sign yields a zero by cancellation.

value.rationale: The permanent’s exact 2-adic valuation for all 2^n sign patterns at every dyadic order is a natural structural invariant, not an arbitrary finite slice. Orbit-stabilizer divisibility gives an infinite combinatorial explanation and a genuinely new contrast between cyclic-displacement and unrestricted matching Fourier operators.

final_claim: For every dyadic n=2^k, k≥1, permanent of any real ±1 circulant C is congruent to n! modulo 2^n, so it has exact valuation n-1 and cannot vanish; hence the cyclic displacement-parity perfect-matching Walsh convolution is invertible with inverse ℓ² bound 2^(1−n), unlike unrestricted matching Fourier transform.
limitations: Only n=2^k circulants with real ±1; lower bound on multiplier magnitude, not sharp inverse norm.
